verdicts.title: A Constructive Proof of Cut Elimination for a System of Full Second Order Logic
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: In this paper we present a constructive proof of cut elimination for a system of full second order logic with the structural rules absorbed and using sets instead of sequences. The standard problem of the cutrank growth is avoided by using a new parameter for the induction, the cutweight. This technique can also be applied to first order logic.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract discusses cut elimination for a system of full second order logic, which shares vocabulary with resolution proof complexity, but does not interact with the specific claim about Φ(π) growth on 3-regular Tseitin formulas under min-occurrence DP elimination.

verdicts.title: Proof Complexity of Symbolic QBF Reasoning
verdicts.abstract_excerpt:
We introduce and investigate symbolic proof systems for Quantified Boolean Formulas (QBF) operating on Ordered Binary Decision Diagrams (OBDDs). These systems capture QBF solvers that perform symbolic quantifier elimination, and as such admit short proofs of formulas of bounded path-width and quantifier complexity. verdicts.title: Cut elimination for propositional cyclic proof systems with fixed-point operators
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: Infinitary and cyclic proof systems are proof systems for logical formulas with fixed-point operators or inductive definitions. A cyclic proof system is a restriction of the corresponding infinitary proof system. Hence, these proof systems are generally not the same, as in the cyclic system may be weaker than the infinitary system.
